reason: The core defect is real. With no header or with the default IN region, the bare ticker AMAL binds to BSE Amal Ltd even though /resolve returns two confidence-1.0 candidates with needs_disambiguation=false. The frontend sends only the global settings region (sidecar-client.ts:172-174), and getQuote/getFundamentals pass only the symbol (sidecar-client.ts:267, :294), so a panel cannot address NASDAQ:AMAL in an IN session. Two corrections. First, a region override does exist: every data route honours the X-Vysted-Region header through _RegionMiddleware and config.get_region (app.py:308-310, config.py:65-77), and with 'X-Vysted-Region: US' both /quotes/AMAL and /fundamentals/AMAL return correct Amalgamated data. What is missing is a per-instrument override, not any override at all. Second, the numbers are not unlabelled: /fundamentals names 'Amal Ltd' and Basic Materials in INR, and the equity panel renders fundamentals.name and quote.currency (EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:993-1002). The user sees another company's correct data under its own name. That is a silent wrong bind with no chooser (high), not the wrong-company-numbers-as-true mixing that DAT-P9-1 shows (critical).

reason: The missing region guard is real, but the cited surface is the wrong one. The /disclosures REST routes have no frontend caller (grep of src/ finds none). The routes and their agent tools are documented India-only (disclosures.py:1, catalog.py:657, :688), and for them 'AMAL' can only mean the BSE listing. The concrete wrong-company leak sits in research. ownership_check.is_applicable decides by bare-ticker NSE/BSE master membership, not by the bound instrument's region (ownership_check.py:94-104), and is_applicable('AMAL') is True. For a US-bound AMAL, the /fundamentals symbol comes back as 'AMAL' with held_percent_insiders 0.386, so fast.py:343-355 fetches Amal Ltd's BSE shareholding. semantics.py:560-575 then surfaces 'Promoter group (exchange filing)' 71.35% as a fact for Amalgamated and raises a false ownership conflict. Wrong money-relevant data is shown as true, so critical holds. The fix belongs in the applicability gate (use the bound instrument's region or exchange), not only in the REST routes.
evidence_checked: Opened the disclosures router, the disclosure agent tools and their catalog descriptions, ownership_check, the research FAST ownership fan-out and the semantics ownership leg. Grepped src/ for /disclosures callers and found none. Called is_applicable in-process. Ran live repros on :52152. The full research drive was not run; the path was confirmed from code plus the live inputs to each gate.
repro_check: curl -H 'X-Vysted-Region: US' /disclosures/shareholding?symbol=AMAL -> promoter 71.35, source BSE, xbrl 506597. curl -H 'X-Vysted-Region: US' /fundamentals/AMAL -> symbol 'AMAL', held_percent_insiders 0.386. sidecar/.venv python: ownership_check.is_applicable('AMAL') -> True, so the research ownership leg would attach Amal Ltd's SHP to Amalgamated.

reason: The field is not unreachable. The app's US earnings surface serves it: /earnings/upcoming?watchlist=AMAL returns scheduled_date 2026-10-22 for 'Amalgamated Financial Corp.', which matches the pack's next_earnings_date, and /earnings/AMAL/history and /earnings/AMAL/estimates return real USD rows. /disclosures/results is documented as an NSE-only results calendar (disclosures.py:74-76) and has no frontend caller. Its message, that 'AMAL' is not a known NSE instrument, is literally true of NASDAQ:AMAL. The research consumer already wraps it as a soft, non-fatal miss (research/disclosures.py:185-203). The Indian listing's NSE gap is DAT-P9-2's finding, not this one.

reason: The gap is real. The Fundamentals model has dividend_per_share and dividend_yield with no declared, record, ex or pay date (models/fundamentals.py:73-74). No router or catalog tool serves splits, bonus, buyback or AGM corporate actions. The only record_date lane reads the NSE corporate-actions feed (dividend_actions.py:12-13), so for a US name no declared-dividend date exists anywhere. Correction: dividend_per_share_ttm is not structurally null. The research FAST path fills it from paid history with an honest paid, affirmed-zero or unavailable label (fast.py:206-230). It is null only on the plain /fundamentals REST response.

reason: The finding holds as stated. The model carries only the scalars fifty_two_week_high, fifty_two_week_low and fifty_two_week_change, with no date for either leg (models/fundamentals.py:77-79). FieldMeta.as_of is documented as the provider's info fetch time. A live US-region fetch shows the 52w high, the 52w low and market_cap all stamped with the same fetch instant. The values themselves are correct (51.59 / 25.13), so low is the right severity.
